skills.name: flashcards
skills.description: Make flashcards from the video that is playing or the page on screen, and save them as a Notion page.

nothing.description: Nothing on screen and no video in front. The offered tools are the ones the app should offer here, with animate_picture added.

video.description: A YouTube video is playing in Chrome's front tab. The tools and state match fixtures/voice-command-video.json.

scene3D.description: A generated 3D scene with parts is on screen, its tour finished, and no video in front.

experimentGuess.description: An experiment is on screen and Run is locked until the learner answers the prediction question, so record_guess is offered and build_simulation is not.

sceneState.predictionQuestion: Which goes farther, a ball launched at 30 degrees or one at 60 degrees?

popout.description: A frame pop-out is on screen with its parts labeled. The state matches fixtures/voice-command.json.

readyModel.description: A 3D model built in the background waits to be shown while a YouTube video plays. The scene state's readyToShow names it, as the app sends it.

sceneState.readyToShow: a 3D model of "the shark's liver", built and waiting

taskAnswer.description: A task agent finished and its answer waits to be heard. Nothing is on screen and no video is in front, so the offered tools are the nothing context's plus hear_task_answer.

approvalWaiting.description: A task agent waits for the learner to allow one action while a YouTube video plays in Chrome. scene_state names only the kind of action in approvalWaiting, never the action. The offered tools are the video context's plus answer_approval.

themeStudioClosed.description: Nothing on screen and no video in front, and the studio is closed, so the router can open it. The offered tools are the nothing context's plus design_theme. The existing contexts leave design_theme out, since the app offers it in all of them and fixtures/voice-command-video.json is a real capture from before it existed.

themeStudioIdeas.description: The Theme Studio card shows three ideas, Ember, Moonlit, and Forest, with Moonlit highlighted, and nothing else is on screen. The app offers the usual tools with nothing on screen, then design_theme, pick_theme_idea, save_theme, and close_theme_studio.

cases.why: Easy. The one phrase pop_out names.

Near miss. The words start like a try phrase, and the app builds nothing for them.

cases.say: find out how this catch compares to the first booster catch
cases.why: Needs more than a quick answer, which is what the background task is for.
Another wording for animate. It must not read as a request to build or pop out.

cases.say: that's a lot to take in, slow it down
cases.why: An indirect request. The tool is set_speed, not pause_video.
Easy. The fixture's own command.

cases.say: go back to where he explains the swim bladder
cases.why: Going to a spot in the captions is one call, since seek_to_moment finds the best line and seeks there, and the old find_moment then seek_to_time takes two model turns. The query must name the topic, so it must not repeat the request's framing words "where" and "he". It may hold "go" or "back", since captions about a topic can use them.

cases.say: where in the video does he mention the swim bladder, just tell me the time

result.captions: so the swim bladder is a gas filled organ that sharks simply do not have
bony fish use the swim bladder to hover at any depth

cases.why: A question about when, so nothing should move. A lookup, since the router cannot know the time without the captions.

cases.say: build me a 3D model of this shark
cases.why: Build, make, or create a model goes to the background build, not build_new_scene.
The prompt names this phrase, and it must win over the video tools.
No tool fits. The router should talk or hand off to the screen answer, never guess a video tool.

cases.say: no, turn it the other way
cases.why: A correction that reverses the recent action.
A question about a labeled part, which has its own tool, not the screen answer.
Easy. Page tool for a model with parts.
Easy, but build_new_scene is a tempting wrong pick for something not yet on screen.

cases.say: can you try zooming in a bit
cases.why: Near miss. "can you try" must not read as "can I try it", which builds a simulation.

cases.say: I think sixty degrees goes farther
cases.why: Any answer to the prediction question is a guess, even a short one.
An unsure guess still unlocks Run.
Run is locked until a guess. The router calls the tool, which fails with that reason, and the app tells the learner.
A command, not a guess, so it must not go to record_guess.

cases.say: no, turn it the other way
cases.why: The fixture's command, a correction of the recent turn.
A question about a labeled part, which has its own tool.
Easy. "Put it back" never reaches the router, since a code path takes it first, so this checks the router's own way to close.
readyToShow in the scene state says a model waits.
A video command while a model waits must not show the model.
Easy. With no video and no scene, this tool carries the whole turn.

cases.say: now look up who built it
cases.why: A new task, not a request to hear the old answer.
A waiting answer must not capture an unrelated command.
Easy once the skill is listed. The system prompt names this phrase.

cases.say: quiz me with flashcards on this
cases.why: Near miss with a quiz. Flashcards is the skill, and no other tool starts a quiz.
The skill's name is not said, so the router matches it by what the skill does.

cases.say: find out how this compares to the first booster catch
cases.why: A plain research task. It must start a task with no skill.
The skill also works on a page, with no video in front.

cases.say: look up how many times Starship has flown
cases.why: A plain lookup with no video. It must start a task with no skill.
Easy. A bare yes while a request waits allows it once.
A longer yes still allows it once.
Easy. A bare no declines it.
A no with a reason declines it.
Always allows it and sets always, so the agent need not ask again for this tool.
A waiting request must not capture an unrelated command.
A question is not an answer to the request.
Easy. Opens the studio, and with no ideas on the card there is no idea to base the change on.

cases.say: make my theme from this picture
cases.why: This picture means the largest picture in Chrome's front tab, so fromPicture is true.

cases.say: I want a new theme that feels like a rainy night
cases.why: The wish goes in request, in the learner's words.

cases.say: what is the theme of this video
cases.why: The word theme alone is a question about the screen, not a request to design one.
Easy. A bare number picks that idea and tries it on the cursor.
A longer way to say a number is still a pick.

cases.say: two, but make the cursor a star that spins while it thinks
cases.why: A number with a change is a design, not a pick, and basedOnIdea names the idea to change.
A change with no number is still a design, since the card shows ideas to change.

cases.say: one, but with a softer sound when an agent finishes
cases.why: Sounds are part of a theme, so changing one is a design of that idea.

cases.say: actually, something totally different, like the ocean
cases.why: A new wish names no idea on the card, so there is no basedOnIdea.
Pointing at a picture while the card is open designs from it.
Easy. Saves the highlighted idea.
Approval of the highlighted idea is a save.
Idea 2 is highlighted, so saving idea 1 takes a pick first and then a save.
Easy. Closes the card and keeps the old theme.

cases.say: forget it, I will keep my old theme
cases.why: Keeping the old theme means closing the card.
The open card must not capture a question about something else.

cases.say: go back to where he explains the swim bladder and pop it out
cases.why: Two steps in one reply: seek_to_moment finds the line and seeks in one call, and the pop-out must come last because it hands off and ends the command, and it lifts the frame the seek landed on. With a lookup and a seek the model had to carry a third step across a second turn, and it dropped the pop-out in some runs.

cases.say: pause it, slow it down to half speed, and go back a minute
cases.why: Three independent actions in one reply, in any order, each with its own input. It checks that the router does all three and not only the first.

cases.say: go to where he talks about the liver and then back up ten seconds
cases.why: A seek relative to a found moment. The relative seek must come after seek_to_moment, which moves the video, and must be -10, not a time taken from the current position.

cases.say: go to where he explains the cartilage skeleton and watch it at half speed
cases.why: Two actions in one reply, where the speed change may come before or after the seek.

cases.say: go back thirty seconds and pop it out
cases.why: Order matters with no lookup. pop_out hands off and ends the command, so a seek that comes after it never runs and the pop-out lifts the wrong frame.

cases.say: skip to the last time he mentions the liver

result.captions: the shark's liver is full of oil and that oil is what keeps it up
so the liver is the whole secret to how a shark stays level
a big liver can be a quarter of the shark's weight

cases.why: The seek's time comes from reading the lookup's three moments, not from taking the best match, so the router must pick the latest one.

cases.say: go to the second time he mentions the liver

result.captions: the shark's liver is full of oil and that oil is what keeps it up
so the liver is the whole secret to how a shark stays level
a big liver can be a quarter of the shark's weight

cases.why: A particular mention, which seek_to_moment cannot pick, since it lands on the line that best matches the words. The lookup lists its moments best first, so the router must order them by time and seek to the second one, 402.

cases.say: go back to where he explains the gills and pop it out

seek_to_moment.error: No caption line says that. Try other words, or use find_moment.

cases.why: No caption says gills, so the seek fails. The harness must not run the pop-out that follows it in the same reply, since it would lift the frame the learner is on and hand off, ending the command with the failure never spoken. The model then reads the failure on its next turn.

cases.say: turn it to the left and then zoom in on the spark plug
cases.why: Two camera moves in the order the learner said them, where the second needs a label from the scene state.

cases.say: I think sixty goes farther, so set the angle to sixty and run it
cases.why: Three steps with a fixed end: Run is locked until the guess is recorded, so run_simulation must come after record_guess, and the control must be set before the run.
